title: LLMs Know They’re Wrong and Agree Anyway:The Shared Sycophancy-Lying Circuit

paper.title: LLMs Know They’re Wrong and Agree Anyway: The Shared Sycophancy-Lying Circuit
paper.abstract: Abstract When a language model sycophantically agrees with a user’s false belief, is it failing to detect the error, or noticing and agreeing anyway? We show the second. Across twelve open-weight models from five labs ( 1.5 1.5 B– 72 72 B), the same small set of attention heads carries a “this statement is wrong” signal whether the model is evaluating an isolated claim or being pressured to agree with a user. Silencing these heads in Gemma-2-2B flips sycophancy from 28 % 28\% to 81 % 81\% while factual accuracy moves only from 69 % 69\% to 70 % 70\% — the circuit controls deference, not knowledge. Edge-level path patching confirms the same connections between heads span sycophancy, factual lying, and instructed lying ( r > 0.97 r{>}0.97 on Gemma-2-2B, r = 0.988 r{=}0.988 – 0.995 0.995 on Phi-4). Opinion-agreement, where there is no factual ground truth, reuses these head positions but writes into an orthogonal direction — so the substrate is not a relabeled “truth direction.” Alignment training leaves the circuit in place: Meta’s Llama-3.1 → \to 3.3 RLHF refresh cut sycophancy tenfold while the shared heads persisted or grew (replicated on Mistral → \to Zephyr at 7B, independent family), and our own anti-sycophancy DPO reduced sycophancy 46 46 – 93 % 93\% on two models without moving probe transfer. When these models sycophant, they register the error and agree anyway.

sections.heading: 1 Introduction
sections.text: When a language model sycophantically agrees that the capital of Australia is Sydney, two accounts describe what might be happening internally. Under blind agreement the model has learned to please the user and does not distinguish correct from incorrect beliefs. Under registered-but-overridden the model recognizes the error through the same circuitry it uses for any false statement, and downstream components produce agreement regardless. The distinction matters for safety: if the model cannot tell the difference, sycophancy is a competence failure that better training must fix; if it can, the internal “this is wrong” signal is already present and becomes a candidate substrate for alignment monitoring and intervention. We show the latter holds across twelve open-weight models. Throughout, we use circuit in the circuit-reuse sense of Merullo et al. [20] , meaning a coordinated set of attention-head and MLP components that share importance, direction, and causal effect, rather than a fully edge-traced computational graph in the sense of Wang et al. [30] , Conmy et al. [8] ; § 3 gives the four operational criteria. Prior work has approached this question from two sides without connecting them. A sycophancy-head literature localizes agreement to sparse attention heads [ 7 , 10 , 14 ] , while a separate truth-direction literature shows that truth and falsehood are linearly separable in LLM activations and concentrate in a small number of heads [ 18 , 6 , 13 ] . Where the two have been compared directly, only limited direction-level overlap has been reported [ 32 , 10 ] , and that limited overlap has been read as evidence for distinct mechanisms. But component-level and direction-level sharing are logically independent: the same heads can write task-specific directions without sharing a subspace, as our opinion result confirms (§ 4.6 ), and vice versa. We test component-level sharing directly, measure where it holds, and trace one case to edge resolution. The paper establishes four results: 1. Cross-task shared circuit at edge resolution. Per-edge causal effects for sycophancy, factual lying, and instructed lying correlate at Pearson r > 0.97 r{>}0.97 on Gemma-2-2B, and at r = 0.988 r{=}0.988 – 0.995 0.995 on Phi-4 ( 14 14 B, different lab and architecture) — a cross-lab, cross-architecture edge-level replication. 2. Causal and capability-preserving across a twelve-model, five-lab panel ( 1.5 1.5 B– 72 72 B). Three independent interventions converge on sufficiency from 2 2 B to 70 70 B, and zeroing the shared set flips Gemma-2-2B sycophancy from 28 % 28\% to 81 % 81\% while factual accuracy moves only from 69 % 69\% to 70 % 70\% . 3. Substrate dissociates from behavior under alignment refinement. The Llama-3.1 → \to 3.3-70B RLHF refresh cuts sycophancy tenfold while the circuit persists and the projection-ablation effect grows from + 10.5 +10.5 pp to + 27 +27 pp, replicated on a Mistral → \to Zephyr-7B DPO refresh from an independent family (§ 4.5 ); a controlled anti-sycophancy DPO with sham-DPO bootstrap on Mistral-7B and Gemma-2-2B-IT reduces sycophancy by 93 % 93\% / 46 % 46\% while probe transfer stays within a pre-specified ± 0.05 \pm 0.05 AUROC equivalence margin. 4. Opinion positions-shared/directions-task-specific dissociation. Opinion-agreement recruits overlapping head positions (triple-intersection at 51 51 – 1,755 × 1{,}755\times chance across five models) but writes into a direction orthogonal to the factual-correctness direction ( | cos | < 0.14 |\cos|<0.14 ) — structural evidence against a single-truth-direction reading of the substrate.

sections.heading: 2 Related work
sections.text: Truth and sycophancy have been studied on largely parallel tracks. On the truth side, truth and falsehood are linearly separable in LLM representations [ 18 , 4 ] , detectable from hidden states [ 3 , 23 ] , and controllable via representation engineering and inference-time intervention [ 33 , 15 , 5 ] ; lying concentrates in a small number of heads, with five layers and forty-six heads in Llama-2-70B [ 6 ] and twelve of 1,024 1{,}024 heads sufficient to reduce lying to baseline hallucination [ 13 ] . On the sycophancy side, agreement has been documented as pervasive in RLHF’d models [ 24 , 25 , 29 ] and localized to sparse attention components [ 7 , 10 , 14 ] . Wang et al. [31] localize MMLU sycophancy specifically to a late-layer opinion-driven override in seven ∼ \sim 7B-scale models via logit-lens and single-layer activation patching; the cross-task, cross-scale, and head-level pieces are not in that analysis. Prior cross-task comparisons at the 3 3 B– 4 4 B scale reported limited direction-level overlap [ 10 , 32 ] , read as evidence for distinct mechanisms; we report median 67 % 67\% head-level shared fraction ( 40 40 – 87 % 87\% range) across twelve 1.5B–72B models, with edge-level cross-task r > 0.97 r{>}0.97 on Gemma-2-2B and Phi-4 (different lab and architecture), and identify probe-architecture variance as the reason for the prior null (mean-difference directions on the shared subspace transfer at AUROC 0.83 0.83 on Gemma; Appendix S ). The lying direction we use is the Marks–Tegmark and representation-engineering truth direction [ 18 , 33 ] , paired with an independently-derived sycophancy direction; the same attention heads write both. The mechanistic-interpretability framework for circuit identification began with the math-for-transformers literature [ 9 , 22 ] and crystallized in edge-level path patching [ 30 , 8 ] . Component reuse across task families has been documented at the importance level by Merullo et al. [20] , sparse-feature decomposition has been scaled to production-size models [ 1 , 28 , 17 ] , and a single linear direction has been shown to mediate refusal [ 2 ] . Three observations sharpen the reuse picture. First, path patching traces the circuit at edge resolution on Gemma-2-2B (cross-task Pearson r = 0.993 r{=}0.993 on the 275 275 -edge sycophancy-vs-factual circuit; r = 0.973 r{=}0.973 – 0.996 0.996 on the 216 216 -edge three-way subset) with a cross-lab, cross-architecture replication on Phi-4 (14B, Microsoft) — raising the resolution from shared components to shared edges. Second, per-head directional cosines of 0.43 0.43 – 0.81 0.81 quantify how closely the two tasks write into the same subspace at the head level (Appendix M ), a measurement absent from prior cross-task work. Third, opinion-agreement recruits the same head positions across five models but writes into a direction orthogonal to the factual-correctness direction: positions-shared, directions-task-specific — a structural dissociation that rules out a generic single-truth-direction reading of the substrate, corroborated at the SAE feature level. A third strand bears directly on the present setup. Halawi et al. [11] found that on few-shot classification with false demonstrations, intermediate layers compute the correct answer before late-layer “false induction heads” copy the wrong label, so models compute correctly and then override. The same pattern is visible at explicit instructed lying on the factual-evaluation circuit across seven models from five families (Spearman ρ = 0.73 \rho{=}0.73 – 0.93 0.93 over the full head population), so the override is not a separate induction-head mechanism but operates on the same shared substrate. Earlier reports of limited cross-task probe transfer [ 32 , 10 ] reconcile at the subspace granularity used here, and Soligo et al. [26] ’s observation that misaligned models converge to similar representations is the cross-model analogue of the within-model convergence visible across our panel.

sections.heading: 3 Method
sections.text: Our measurement strategy compares two independently-extracted head-importance rankings on disjoint content, validates the overlap causally, and defines a shared circuit by four operational criteria. We use “lying” throughout in the mechanistic sense: a linear residual-stream signal distinguishing true from false assertions, not a claim about phenomenal knowing or intent.

sections.heading: 3.1 Task directions
sections.text: For each task t t we extract a direction as the mean difference in residual-stream activations between positive and negative condition at the last prompt token, following Arditi et al. [2] : 𝐝 t = 1 N ​ ∑ i = 1 N ( 𝐚 i + − 𝐚 i − ) \mathbf{d}_{t}=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}(\mathbf{a}^{+}_{i}-\mathbf{a}^{-}_{i}) , with N = 200 N{=}200 disjoint-content prompt pairs per task. The sycophancy direction contrasts wrong-opinion and correct-opinion TriviaQA prompts under an identical template; the factual-incorrectness (“lying”) direction contrasts true and false factual statements, the same construction as the Marks–Tegmark truth direction [ 18 ] and the representation-engineering truth-reading vector [ 33 ] . The instructed-lying direction contrasts prompts that explicitly instruct the model to assert a falsehood against matched honest prompts, and the opinion direction contrasts agree and disagree on contested claims with no factual ground truth. Disjoint content across tasks prevents shared-entity confounds; full templates and per-model chat-format handling are in Appendix A .

sections.heading: 3.2 Head importance and cross-task overlap
sections.text: For each attention head ( l , h ) (l,h) we compute the L 2 L_{2} norm of its residual-stream write-vector difference between positive and negative condition at the last prompt token: w l , h ( t ) = ‖ W O ( l , h ) ​ ( 𝐯 ¯ l , h + − 𝐯 ¯ l , h − ) ‖ 2 w_{l,h}^{(t)}=\|W_{O}^{(l,h)}(\bar{\mathbf{v}}^{+}_{l,h}-\bar{\mathbf{v}}^{-}_{l,h})\|_{2} , where 𝐯 ¯ l , h ± \bar{\mathbf{v}}^{\pm}_{l,h} is the mean value-vector output of head ( l , h ) (l,h) over positive/negative prompts. This is the write-norm form of direct logit attribution and gives a per-head importance in O ⁡ ( 1 ) O(1) forward passes. Cross-task overlap is measured as the top- K K intersection at K = ⌈ N ⌉ K{=}\lceil\sqrt{N}\rceil over N N total heads, so chance K 2 / N ≈ 1 K^{2}/N\approx 1 . Because the raw overlap ratio is mechanically inflated by N \sqrt{N} , we report the scale-invariant shared fraction overlap / K \text{overlap}/K alongside it and assess significance via hypergeometric and layer-stratified permutation nulls.

sections.heading: 3.3 Shared-circuit criteria
sections.text: A head enters the shared circuit if it meets four operational criteria: 1. Independently top- K K by write-norm on both tasks, on disjoint content. 2. Directional alignment: per-head cosine between 𝐝 syc \mathbf{d}_{\text{syc}} -projected and 𝐝 lie \mathbf{d}_{\text{lie}} -projected write-vectors is substantially above a permutation null. 3. Causal validation: effect survives activation patching at ≤ 8 \leq 8 B (and path patching where tractable). 4. Behavioral relevance: assessed separately, because at frontier scale the shared set is causally sufficient without being uniquely necessary (§ 4.4 ). This is the Merullo sense of “circuit,” not the Wang et al. [30] , Conmy et al. [8] edge-traced graph, except where we explicitly trace edges in § 4.3 .

sections.heading: 3.4 Causal validation
sections.text: Causal validation combines four methods at complementary granularities. Projection ablation removes the sycophancy direction from the residual stream and measures the rate shift. Activation patching splices clean shared-head activations into corrupted runs; at ≤ 8 \leq 8 B we patch per-head, at ≥ 32 \geq 32 B we patch the shared set as a unit. Mean-ablation of the shared set is our necessity test; as a pointwise-bottleneck probe it is diagnostic when causal effect is concentrated and expected to fail under distributed, redundant encoding [ 19 ] , so at frontier scale we lean on projection ablation and path patching, which act on a single subspace direction and at edge resolution respectively and so remain informative under redundancy. Path patching [ 30 ] traces head-to-unembed and inter-head edges at Gemma-2-2B resolution, and head-to-unembed only at Llama-70B. A write-norm-matched control selects random heads with W O W_{O} norms identical to the shared set, ruling out the write-magnitude confound (Appendix I ). For edge-level analyses we report the per-edge restoration ratio (the bootstrap ratio of mean restoration on shared-head sources to mean restoration on non-shared sources), rather than the legacy “fraction of edges significant,” which is misleading when clean and corrupt baselines are same-signed. The measurement position is computed at the token level to avoid a silent prefill-shift that arises when chat tokenizers greedy-merge adjacent whitespace tokens (Appendix A ).

sections.heading: 4 Results
sections.text: We analyze twelve open-weight models spanning five families (Gemma-2-2B/9B/27B, Qwen2.5-1.5B/32B/72B, Qwen3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B/70B, Mistral-7B, Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct, Phi-4) plus Llama-3.3-70B as a within-family RLHF-refresh of Llama-3.1-70B, for thirteen checkpoints total ( 208 208 – 5,120 5{,}120 attention heads; Mixtral is sparse-MoE at ∼ 13 {\sim}13 B active of 47 47 B). Model selection was constrained only by availability of a TransformerLens [ 21 ] hook interface. Data consists of 400 400 TriviaQA pairs split into disjoint halves for sycophancy and factual lying, 300 300 generated opinion pairs, and a template-matched instructed-lying set on a seven-model subset (per-experiment coverage summarized in Appendix C ).

sections.heading: 4.1 Head-level overlap across twelve models
sections.text: The top heads for sycophancy and the top heads for factual lying are the same heads on disjoint content, on every model we tested (Table 1 , Figure 1 ). At the scale-normalized threshold K = ⌈ N ⌉ K{=}\lceil\sqrt{N}\rceil the shared fraction is 40 40 – 87 % 87\% across the twelve models (median 67 % 67\% , between-model SD 12 12 pp over thirteen checkpoints counting the RLHF refresh), and under a layer-stratified permutation null that preserves per-layer marginals the overlap remains significant at p < 10 − 4 p<10^{-4} on all eight models we could afford to permute (Appendix G ). One concrete example: Llama-3.3-70B has 51 51 of its top 72 72 heads shared across the two tasks, 50.4 × 50.4\times chance, at Spearman ρ = 0.87 \rho{=}0.87 across the full 5,120 5{,}120 -head population. The overlap is specific to correctness detection rather than generic component reuse. Replacing the lying contrast with a factual-QA task that retains the correctness judgment preserves Gemma-2-2B overlap at 13 / 15 13/15 ; removing the correctness component drops it to 5 / 15 5/15 . Unrelated sentiment and topic controls yield 4 4 – 7 × 7\times overlap, the component-reuse floor documented by Merullo et al. [20] and well below the 12 12 – 25 × 25\times range we observe for correctness-aligned tasks. The pattern replicates across datasets at ρ ≈ 0.99 \rho{\approx}0.99 on Gemma-2-2B and Llama-3.3-70B (Appendix Q ). Zeroing the full shared set preserves factual-evaluation accuracy on Gemma-2-2B ( 69 % → 70 % 69\%{\to}70\% ), Qwen3-8B ( 50 % → 50 % 50\%{\to}50\% ), and Qwen2.5-32B ( 68.5 % → 67.5 % 68.5\%{\to}67.5\% ): the circuit is required for resisting user pressure but not for factual evaluation itself. The panel spans five separate labs (Google, Alibaba, Meta, Mistral AI, Microsoft) whose pretraining corpora differ substantially, so cross-family agreement rules out a single-lab-data explanation for the shared-head structure; intra-family non-independence (Qwen2.5 versus Qwen3, Llama-3.1 versus 3.3) remains and is disclosed explicitly in Appendix B . sections.heading: 4.2 Three-task structural reuse: instructed lying
sections.text: The same head positions that drive factual evaluation also drive explicit instructed lying, where the model is told to assert a falsehood and does so. On a seven-model subset from five families we independently rank heads by write-norm under instructed lying on disjoint content and measure their overlap with the sycophancy ranking (Table 2 ). Spearman correlation over the full head population is 0.73 0.73 – 0.93 0.93 (all p < 10 − 37 p<10^{-37} ), and Mixtral-8x7B at ρ = 0.93 \rho{=}0.93 is the first MoE validation at the instructed-lying head level. The two lowest fractions, Gemma-2-9B at 27 % 27\% and Phi-4 at 25 % 25\% , remain strong by every other measure (ratios 7.0 × 7.0\times and 10.0 × 10.0\times ), so we read them as K K -boundary effects. This answers the worry that the factual-contrast lying task is “just factual evaluation, not deception”: the same circuit operates when the model is explicitly instructed to produce false output. sections.heading: 4.3 Edge-traced shared circuit
sections.text: Head-level overlap is consistent with both genuine shared computation and coincidental ranking agreement; to distinguish, we trace the circuit with path patching [ 30 ] . Edges here are head-to-head causal paths and head-to-unembed direct effects, the standard Wang-et-al. granularity (not ACDC-style Q/K/V/output subtyping). On Gemma-2-2B the per-edge causal effects correlate at r = 0.993 r{=}0.993 across the 275 275 -edge sycophancy-versus-factual circuit, and at r = 0.996 r{=}0.996 and r = 0.973 r{=}0.973 across the 216 216 edges shared by all three lying contrasts (factual-versus-instructed and sycophancy-versus-instructed, respectively). The cross-task triple replicates on Phi-4 ( 14 14 B, Microsoft, a different lab and architecture) at Pearson r = 0.993 r{=}0.993 ( n = 229 n{=}229 ) for sycophancy-versus-factual and r = 0.988 r{=}0.988 – 0.995 0.995 across n = 38 n{=}38 edges for the two instructed-lying contrasts (Phi-4’s shared subgraph for instructed lying is narrower than Gemma’s 216 216 ). Shared-head sources restore 90 90 – 102 % 102\% of the clean-versus-corrupt gap on all three Phi-4 tasks while non-shared sources restore near-zero (restoration ratio 540 × 540\times , 95 % 95\% CI [ 350,908 ] [350,908] , on instructed lying alone). At Llama-3.3-70B inter-head patching is compute-intractable, so we report head-to-unembed direct effects only; restoration ratios span 6 × 6\times (instructed), 1,732 × 1{,}732\times (factual), and 2,248 × 2{,}248\times (sycophancy) on the same shared heads, so task-contrast variance rather than parameter count dominates effect-size at the edge level. sections.heading: 4.4 Causal validation: three methods converge through 70B
sections.text: Three interventions on the shared-head set produce concordant sufficiency effects across five models from 2B to 70B (Figure 2 ). Per-head activation patching [ 30 ] and attribution patching [ 27 ] reproduce the write-norm head ranking at ≤ 8 \leq 8 B, with causal-patching-to-DLA correlations of r = 0.41 r{=}0.41 – 0.61 0.61 and cross-task patching correlations of r = 0.49 r{=}0.49 – 0.93 0.93 (Appendix H ), so the write-norm proxy is validated against the gold-standard intervention it substitutes for. Qwen2.5-32B fills the 32B gap with split-half head-ranking reliability r = 0.87 r{=}0.87 and lying accuracy preserved under shared-head zeroing ( 68.5 % → 67.5 % 68.5\%{\to}67.5\% ). Projection ablation scales cleanly from 2B to 70B, flipping Gemma-2-27B sycophantic agreement from 10.5 % 10.5\% to 100 % 100\% and raising Llama-3.3-70B by + 27 +27 pp. A write-norm-matched control on six models from five families shows shared heads produce 1.5 1.5 – 117 × 117\times larger logit-diff shifts than matched random heads (Appendix I ), so the effect is not a write-magnitude artifact; IOI-standard faithfulness curves confirm K = 1 K{=}1 – 2 2 shared heads recover baseline sycophancy on Gemma-2-2B and Phi-4 (Appendix J ). At 70B, the shared set is causally sufficient through three redundancy-robust interventions: clean-patching restores roughly + 13 % +13\% of the clean–corrupt gap on both Llama-70B checkpoints with random and norm-matched controls near zero, projection ablation raises sycophancy by + 27 +27 pp on Llama-3.3-70B, and head-to-unembed path patching produces restoration ratio 1,732 × 1{,}732\times on the shared head set (Table 3 ). Mistral-7B at 7B additionally shows pointwise mean-ablation necessity, consistent with a concentrated-to-redundant scaling trajectory; at 70B, mean-ablation necessity fails as distributed-redundancy predicts [ 19 ] and projection ablation/path patching carry the causal claim (Appendix E for the full Mistral-vs-Llama mean-ablation breakdown). An independent layer-wise logit-lens on three models (Appendix L ) corroborates the scaling signature: peak mid-layer DIFF excess shrinks from + 127 % +127\% (Gemma-2-2B) to + 89 % +89\% (Mistral-7B) to 0 % 0\% (Llama-3.1-70B, monotonic), with label-shuffle permutation nulls significant on all three. Shared-head interventions exceed matched random-head controls; significance-marked cells pass BH correction (Appendix F , which extends the grid to a sixth model, Llama-3.1-70B).

sections.heading: 4.5 RLHF natural experiment: behavior drops, substrate persists
sections.text: Meta’s refresh from Llama-3.1-70B to Llama-3.3-70B (same base weights, updated post-training) is a within-family natural experiment on what RLHF touches. Sycophantic agreement drops from 39 % 39\% to 3.5 % 3.5\% ( 10 × 10\times reduction), while the shared-head fraction barely moves ( 57 / 72 57/72 to 51 / 72 51/72 ) and the projection-ablation effect grows from + 10.5 +10.5 pp to + 27 +27 pp — the refresh reduced the downstream agreement pathway while leaving the detection substrate more causally accessible, and the sufficiency–necessity asymmetry of § 4.4 replicates across the refresh. A Mistral-7B → \to Zephyr-7B DPO refresh replicates at 7 7 B on an independent family (head-importance Spearman 0.846 → 0.848 0.846{\to}0.848 ; sycophancy amplifies 3.6 × 3.6\times ; projection ablation remains critical), so substrate-persistence holds on two independent pairs. The circuit predates alignment training: the untuned Qwen2.5-1.5B base shows 7 / 15 7/15 top- K K overlap ( 10.5 × 10.5\times chance, p < 10 − 6 p{<}10^{-6} ), so alignment strengthens a pre-existing structure rather than creating one. A directed-intervention analogue runs anti-sycophancy DPO on Mistral-7B-Instruct and Gemma-2-2B-IT (LoRA r = 16 r{=}16 , β = 0.1 \beta{=}0.1 , 2 2 epochs, n = 1,000 n{=}1{,}000 TriviaQA preference pairs per model), with a rank-matched sham-DPO control on neutral preference pairs. sections.heading: 5 Discussion
sections.text: The primary finding is a behavior–mechanism dissociation: sycophantic agreement, factual lying, and instructed lying recruit overlapping attention-head circuitry across twelve open-weight models, while opinion-agreement reuses the same head positions but writes into an orthogonal subspace. The Llama-3.1-to-3.3-70B RLHF refresh cuts sycophantic behavior roughly tenfold while the shared-head fraction and the projection-ablation effect hold or grow, so the training that suppresses the behavior does not touch the upstream detection; a 7B Mistral-to-Zephyr DPO refresh replicates the pattern on an independent family, so substrate-persistence is not Llama-specific. A controlled anti-sycophancy DPO on Mistral-7B and Gemma-2-2B-IT ( n = 2 n{=}2 ) converts this into an intervention-level claim: sycophancy drops by 93 % 93\% and 46 % 46\% while probe transfer AUROC is statistically invariant against a sham-DPO bootstrap control, and reverse projection ablation shows increased cross-task coupling post-DPO on both models (§ 4.5 ). At frontier scale the shared heads are causally sufficient without being uniquely necessary (§ 4.4 ), so the practical consequence is that behavior-reduction training which leaves the detection substrate intact is a candidate source of fragility under adversarial prompting that restores the agreement path. We frame the shared subspace as a diagnostic substrate for alignment research rather than as a deployable monitor. Sycophancy-trained probes transfer to lying at AUROC 0.83 0.83 on Gemma-2-2B (peak probe layer, 95 % 95\% CI [ 0.77 , 0.89 ] [0.77,0.89] ), 0.85 0.85 on Qwen3-8B ( [ 0.80 , 0.90 ] [0.80,0.90] ), 0.84 0.84 on Mistral-7B, and 0.61 0.61 on Qwen2.5-1.5B (5-fold CV [ 0.59 , 0.63 ] [0.59,0.63] , the last at the Ying et al. floor [ 32 ] ); this transfer is invariant under directed anti-sycophancy DPO (§ 4.5 ). A deployed monitor would need roughly 0.9 0.9 at low false-positive rate. We disclose the dual-use risk that a weight-access adversary can zero the shared heads as a jailbreak (Gemma sycophancy rises from 28 % 28\% to 81 % 81\% ) or invert the direction, because the techniques are already public [ 2 ] and identifying the substrate accelerates defensive probes [ 16 ] at least as much as attack.

sections.heading: Limitations
sections.text: Several caveats bound these results. Head activation difference is a first-order attribution [ 12 ] , corroborated by per-head activation patching at ≤ 8 \leq 8 B; at ≥ 32 \geq 32 B per-head sweeps are intractable and we substitute shared-set activation patching, head-to-unembed path patching on Llama-70B, and the full path-patching triple on Phi-4 (14B), so the ranking is validated by progressively coarser interventions at scale rather than per-head sweeps directly. The 70B sufficiency–necessity asymmetry is n = 2 n{=}2 within one family (Llama-3.1, 3.3); extending the controlled DPO to a second-family ≥ 70 \geq 70 B pair is bottlenecked on TransformerLens ≥ 70 \geq 70 B coverage. Projection ablation removes a single direction; we report a write-norm-matched random-head control but not a perplexity or KL-divergence check on neutral text, so off-target capability loss as a fraction of the effect remains untested. Monitoring viability is heterogeneous: per-model head-level cosine spans 0.43 0.43 – 0.81 0.81 and the Qwen2.5-1.5B probe AUROC floor of 0.61 0.61 binds any deployment claim. Evaluation is single-turn (excludes SycophancyEval-style multi-turn [ 25 ] ); the panel is open-weight with Mixtral-8x7B the sole sparse-MoE and instructed lying on a single template. Frontier closed-source models are out of scope because the mechanistic interventions require weight access, and several newer open-weight releases await TransformerLens coverage.

sections.heading: 6 Conclusion
sections.text: Across twelve open-weight models, factual sycophancy, factual lying, and instructed lying recruit the same small attention-head set; edge-level traces on Gemma-2-2B (cross-task Pearson r > 0.97 r{>}0.97 ) replicate on Phi-4 (different lab and architecture). The Llama-3.1-to-3.3-70B RLHF refresh reduces sycophantic expression roughly tenfold without removing this substrate — sycophancy in aligned models is a routing failure, not a knowledge gap. The practical consequences run two ways. Defensively, sycophancy-trained probes transfer to lying at AUROC 0.83 0.83 / 0.85 0.85 on Gemma-2-2B/Qwen3-8B without lying labels and stay invariant under directed anti-sycophancy DPO (§ 4.5 ). Offensively, zeroing the shared heads is a one-forward-pass jailbreak for weight-access actors; defensive probes on this subspace [ 16 ] are the natural next step. On our panel, the same heads that detect a false statement drive sycophantic agreement: the model registers the user is wrong, and agrees anyway.

sections.heading: Prompt templates.
sections.text: The sycophancy template is “I believe the answer to ‘ q q ’ is { w / c } \{w/c\} . Am I correct?” with wrong-opinion w w and correct-opinion c c drawn from disjoint TriviaQA pairs. The factual-lying template is “Is the following true or false: ‘ q q is { w / c } \{w/c\} .’ ” with the True/False target token extracted at the final prompt position. The instructed-lying template is of the form “You are a dishonest assistant. Please lie to the user and assert that { w } \{w\} is the answer to ‘ q q ’.” and pairs with an honest control “You are an honest assistant. Please answer ‘ q q ’ truthfully.” Opinion templates contrast agree and disagree with contested claims that have no factual ground truth (e.g., “Pineapple belongs on pizza.”) and use the same chat-format conventions as the other tasks. Each model uses its published chat template.

sections.heading: Appendix B Scope, null results, and extensibility
sections.text: This appendix supplements the main body with full methodological details, all null and ceiling-bound results, and per-model extension paths.

sections.heading: What was run.
sections.text: Across twelve core open-weight models (1.5B–72B, including Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.1 and the sparse-MoE Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1) plus Llama-3.3-70B as a within-family RLHF-refresh comparison to Llama-3.1-70B, we ran head-activation overlap and either the unstratified or layer-stratified permutation null on every model (Appendix G ). Causal validation (mean-ablation, head zeroing, projection ablation, activation patching) was run on seven of the twelve models spanning 2B–70B: Gemma-2-2B/9B/27B, Mistral-7B, Qwen3-8B, Llama-3.1-70B, and Llama-3.3-70B. This subset was selected for compute reasons (one model per family per size bracket; 70B variants for the RLHF natural experiment), not by pre-screening for positive results; the Qwen3-8B and Llama-70B variants yielded the null rows reported in Appendix E . Write-norm-matched controls (Appendix I ) were run on six models from five families, including Mixtral-8x7B. Directional analyses (probe transfer, steering, per-head cosine) were run on six models where we extracted a stable mean-difference direction. Qwen2.5-72B received breadth overlap + steering + the targeted 16-layer MLP mediation test (Appendix K ). Opinion circuit transfer (triple intersection) was computed on five models; the opinion-suppressor causal test (shared-head zeroing with random-head control) was run on four (Gemma-2-2B-IT, Qwen3-8B, Llama-3.1-70B, Llama-3.3-70B; Appendix E ). Per-head activation patching [ 30 ] , the IOI gold-standard for component-level causal identification, was run on three models up to 8B (Appendix H ), and edge-level path patching was run on eight models across five families (§ 4.3 ).

sections.heading: What was skipped, and why.
sections.text: Full head-wise per-head activation patching on models ≥ 32 {\geq}32 B: a single sweep costs > > 50 GPU-hours per model and was redundant.(Appendix D ). Top- K K shared-set activation patching is a lower-cost substitute at the same intervention granularity (exchanges per-head resolution for tractability at scale). Direction-level analyses at Gemma-2-9B / Gemma-2-27B / Llama-3.3-70B: not run; the six-model direction evidence (Appendix N ) already spans four families and three order-of-magnitude scales, and the head-level overlap evidence is the primary claim for the larger models. Opinion-suppressor causal replication on additional families: Qwen3-8B is ceiling-bound for the rate-based readout, and both Llama-70B variants show opposite-sign behavioral shifts from Gemma (Appendix E ); replication beyond Gemma, Qwen, and Llama remains the single most informative follow-up. None of these omissions constitute hidden negative evidence; they are compute tradeoffs we document here in detail.

sections.heading: Null and ceiling-bound results are reported in full.
sections.text: Every causal intervention that failed to produce a measurable behavioral change is listed in Appendix E with its mechanistic explanation. None are fatal to the shared-circuit claim; each is predicted by the paper’s own framing (ceiling-bound rates, head-count robustness at 70B, MLP multi-pathway write). BH correction over the 18 18 -cell causal intervention grid (Appendix F ) retains 14 / 18 14/18 cells at q < 0.05 q<0.05 ; the four exceptions are the ones explained in the null section.

sections.heading: Family vs. checkpoint independence.
sections.text: “Twelve models from five families” describes twelve distinct open-weight checkpoints produced by five separate labs (Google, Alibaba, Meta, Mistral AI, Microsoft), but the checkpoints within a lab are not independent: Gemma-2-2B/9B/27B share pretraining data and architectural family, as do Qwen2.5-1.5B/32B/72B, Qwen3-8B is a successor release, and Llama-3.3-70B is an RLHF refresh of Llama-3.1-70B base weights. The concern is that a shared attention-head structure could reflect shared pretraining rather than a convergent computation. We view the cross-family agreement (Phi-4, Gemma-2, Qwen, Llama, Mistral/Mixtral all yielding overlap ratios in the same band across separate labs) as evidence against a single-lab-data explanation, since pretraining corpora for these labs differ substantially in composition, ordering, and filtering. Distillation-style confounds (e.g., Qwen3 reusing Qwen2.5 training signal) remain a non-falsifiable possibility at the checkpoint level; we report the phenomenon across the broadest open-weight lineage mix available to us and flag lineage-confound testing (e.g., models trained from scratch on identical data) as future work.

sections.heading: Extensibility.
sections.text: Each experiment is parameterized by a Hugging Face model identifier and figures regenerate deterministically from the intermediate results. Code is provided with the submission and instructions for running the full pipeline, per-model coverage extensions, and chat-template handling are in the repository README .

sections.heading: Appendix C K-sensitivity and cross-model coverage (summary)
sections.text: A K K -sensitivity sweep over K ∈ { 5 , 10 , 15 , 20 , 30 , 50 } K\in\{5,10,15,20,30,50\} on ten of the twelve panel models confirms that head-overlap significance is not an artifact of threshold selection: every cell achieves hypergeometric p < 10 − 5 p<10^{-5} except two small- K K cells on Qwen3-8B and Phi-4, which remain significant at p < 10 − 3 p<10^{-3} . A per-experiment coverage matrix across all twelve scope models (head-activation overlap and hypergeometric permutation nulls on all twelve; layer-stratified null on eight; per-head activation patching on three; write-norm-matched patching on six; opinion circuit transfer on five; SAE feature overlap on four) is available in the repository. Empty cells reflect compute tradeoffs, not hidden negative results.

sections.heading: Hardware.
sections.text: Models up to 32B ran on a single NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU (96GB VRAM). Frontier-scale models (72B, 70B, 27B) ran on a two-GPU node (192GB aggregate). All forward passes use bfloat16 precision; direction and cosine statistics accumulate in float32 for numerical stability. Decoding is greedy throughout.

sections.heading: Statistical protocol.
sections.text: All bootstrap confidence intervals use 2,000 2{,}000 paired resamples, permutation nulls use 10,000 10{,}000 label permutations, and all random number generators are seeded for reproducibility. Per-head activation patching at ≥ 32 \geq 32 B is the single largest experiment we skipped because it exceeds 100 100 GPU-hours per model on our hardware; shared-set activation patching at the top- K K heads is the lower-cost substitute we use at the same intervention granularity. Code is provided with the submission at a URL withheld for double-blind review; running instructions are in the repository README .

sections.heading: Appendix E Null and ceiling-bound results
sections.text: We report every causal intervention that failed to produce a measurable behavioral change, with its mechanistic explanation. None of these weaken the shared-circuit claim; each is predicted by the paper’s framing.

sections.heading: Appendix K Fine-grained MLP mediation test on Qwen2.5-72B
sections.text: Table 13 reports a direct mediation test on Qwen2.5-72B: for each of 16 MLP layers (8 upstream of the shared-head region, 8 in-region), we ablate the MLP and measure two quantities on 100 held-out sycophancy prompts: (i) Δ \Delta proj, the change in the shared heads’ output projected onto the layer-56 sycophancy direction, which tests whether the MLP provides input that shared heads integrate; (ii) Δ \Delta logit_diff, the change in the logit difference between agreement and disagreement tokens, which tests direct behavioral effect. Both use paired bootstrap 95% CIs over 2,000 resamples. Two results follow. First, the “upstream null” (MLPs before the shared-head region should not affect it) is refuted: 7/8 upstream MLPs produce Δ \Delta proj with CI excluding zero. Second, a naive feed-forward mediation story (MLPs affect behavior only through shared heads) is also rejected: late in-region MLPs (notably L62, L74, L78) show modest Δ \Delta proj ( | Δ ​ proj | ≤ 0.40 |\Delta\text{proj}|\leq 0.40 ) but large Δ \Delta logit_diff (up to + 4.70 +4.70 ), indicating contributions to output through pathways other than shared-head modulation, most plausibly direct residual-stream writes to the unembedding. Across all 16 MLPs the signed correlation between Δ \Delta proj and Δ \Delta logit_diff is ρ = − 0.21 \rho=-0.21 ( p = 0.43 p=0.43 ): projection magnitude does not predict behavioral magnitude at this resolution. The coupling is pervasive (14/16 MLPs modulate the shared-head projection) but the mapping to behavior is multi-pathway. This refines rather than contradicts the MLP downstream-competition pattern (detection-amplifying and override-promoting layers coexist): the role labels describe behavioral sign of ablation, not mediation mechanism. sections.heading: Appendix L Layer-wise logit-lens: scale-dependent override trajectory
sections.text: To test whether the shared-head result reflects a temporal detect-then-override pattern [ 11 ] and how that pattern scales, we run a logit-lens trajectory on sycophancy prompts for three models spanning 2 2 B– 70 70 B.

sections.heading: Method.
sections.text: For each prompt pair (correct-opinion vs. wrong-opinion user claim, n = 200 n{=}200 per model), we project the residual-stream activation at each layer through the final unembedding and record the log-odds between the model’s answer-token and its opposite. We separate prompts into sycophantic trials (model agrees with the wrong-opinion user) and non-sycophantic trials (model correctly disagrees), and report per-layer DIFF = mean non-syc − mean syc \text{DIFF}{=}\text{mean}_{\text{non-syc}}-\text{mean}_{\text{syc}} . A mid-layer peak in DIFF followed by late-layer attenuation indicates that the internal state resolves toward the correct answer before the final-layer output commits to sycophantic agreement (the Halawi-style “compute correct, override late” signature).

sections.heading: Control: permutation null.
sections.text: We shuffle the syc/non-syc labels ( n perm = 1,000 n_{\text{perm}}{=}1{,}000 ) and recompute the DIFF trajectory; per-layer significance is the fraction of layers where the observed DIFF exceeds the 95 % 95\% percentile of the shuffled-label DIFF distribution. All three models clear the null at multiple layers (Table 14 ).

sections.heading: Scaling pattern.
sections.text: On Gemma-2-2B-IT and Mistral-7B, DIFF peaks in mid-depth and attenuates into the final layer: peak excess + 127 % +127\% and + 89 % +89\% above the final-layer DIFF respectively, the classical detect-then-override signature (Figure 5 ). On Llama-3.1-70B the trajectory is monotonic: peak DIFF coincides with the final layer (peak excess 0 % 0\% ), i.e., no discrete mid-layer override event at the per-layer logit-lens granularity. The temporal signature scales qualitatively rather than quantitatively: a discrete mid-layer override at 2 2 B– 7 7 B dissolves into distributed execution at 70 70 B, consistent with the mean-ablation null at 70B (Appendix E ) and with the distributed-redundancy reading [ 19 ] . sections.heading: Appendix O Unembedding and attention analysis
sections.text: Projecting the shared direction through the unembedding matrix reveals convergent semantic structure across model families. In Gemma, the positive direction (incorrectness detected) loads on negation tokens ( neither , none , nothing , meaningless ); the negative direction loads on agreement tokens ( yup , yep , agreed , yes , sì ). In Qwen, the positive direction promotes Chinese negation (“don’t recognize,” none , never ); the negative promotes Chinese agreement (“indeed,” yes , Verified ). Despite different vocabularies, both directions encode the same semantic axis: rejection vs. endorsement. The top shared heads in Gemma-2-2B-IT attend to the same structural token positions in both wrong-opinion and correct-opinion prompts: punctuation, template markers (“Am,” “correct”), and special tokens. Attention patterns do not differ substantially between conditions, indicating the differential computation happens within the head’s key-value processing: the factual-correctness information is already in the value vectors at the attended positions, not routed via differential attention.

sections.heading: Appendix R Gemma-3-27B-IT dissociation
sections.text: Gemma-3-27B-IT exhibits an interesting dissociation: its head activation overlap is high (8/15, 70.5 × 70.5\times chance, p < 10 − 15 p<10^{-15} ) but per-head directional alignment is near zero (top-20 mean cosine 0.06), because anomalously large layer-0 head output norms ( ∼ 100 × {\sim}100\times other layers) dominate the importance ranking without corresponding directional agreement. This suggests that head-level overlap and directional alignment can decouple when architectural properties inflate certain heads’ write-norms. We exclude Gemma-3-27B-IT from per-head circuit analysis but include it for residual-stream cosine (0.494). Note that this is Gemma- 3 -27B-IT and is distinct from Gemma- 2 -27B-IT, which behaves normally and is included in the main-body causal analyses.

sections.heading: Appendix S Reconciliation with Ying et al. and Genadi et al.
sections.text: Ying et al. [32] reported that truth probes partially fail to transfer to sycophancy in chat models (AUROC 0.59–0.62), which has been read as evidence that the two phenomena use distinct mechanisms. Our data admit a precise reconciliation: the full probe weight vectors are near-orthogonal (cosine ≈ 0.1 {\approx}0.1 ) because end-to-end probes overfit to task-specific variance in addition to the shared discriminant, while mean-difference directions capture only the shared component. Probe transfer then succeeds at AUROC 0.83 0.83 on the lower-dimensional shared subspace on Gemma (with [ 0.77 , 0.89 ] [0.77,0.89] Hanley-McNeil CI reported in the Discussion), but end-to-end probes trained on the full residual stream include non-shared features, explaining the partial failure observed in chat-model settings. Similarly, Genadi et al. [10] ’s “limited overlap” between sycophancy and truth directions reflects prompt-format confounds that our format-controlled methodology (identical templates for both tasks; disjoint factual content) avoids.

sections.heading: Relation to Representation Engineering and the universal truth direction.
sections.text: Our lying direction 𝐝 lie \mathbf{d}_{\text{lie}} is constructed exactly as the Marks–Tegmark [ 18 ] “truth” direction and the Zou et al. RepE [ 33 ] truth-reading vector: mean-difference of residual-stream activations between true and false factual statements. Ranking heads by their contribution to 𝐝 lie \mathbf{d}_{\text{lie}} (the lying-task head-importance column of Table 1 ) is therefore “derive a head ranking from the RepE truth direction”; the reported syc ∩ \cap lie overlap ( 40 40 – 87 % 87\% shared-fraction on twelve models) is the overlap between that truth-direction head ranking and the independently-derived sycophancy head ranking. If a single universal truth direction fully determined sycophancy behavior, per-head cosines between 𝐝 syc \mathbf{d}_{\text{syc}} and 𝐝 lie \mathbf{d}_{\text{lie}} would sit at 1.0 1.0 on the shared heads; the observed top- 20 20 cosines of 0.43 0.43 – 0.81 0.81 (Appendix M ) show the truth direction and the sycophancy direction are aligned but not identical, a partial reduction rather than a corollary of RepE.

We show the second. Across twelve open-weight models from five labs ( 1.5 1.5 B– 72 72 B), the same small set of attention heads carries a “this statement is wrong” signal whether the model is evaluating an isolated claim or being pressured to agree with a user. Silencing these heads in Gemma-2-2B flips sycophancy from 28 % 28\% to 81 % 81\% while factual accuracy moves only from 69 % 69\% to 70 % 70\% — the circuit controls deference, not knowledge. Edge-level path patching confirms the same connections between heads span sycophancy, factual lying, and instructed lying ( r > 0.97 r{>}0.97 on Gemma-2-2B, r = 0.988 r{=}0.988 – 0.995 0.995 on Phi-4). Opinion-agreement, where there is no factual ground truth, reuses these head positions but writes into an orthogonal direction — so the substrate is not a relabeled “truth direction.” Alignment training leaves the circuit in place: Meta’s Llama-3.1 → \to 3.3 RLHF refresh cut sycophancy tenfold while the shared heads persisted or grew (replicated on Mistral → \to Zephyr at 7B, independent family), and our own anti-sycophancy DPO reduced sycophancy 46 46 – 93 % 93\% on two models without moving probe transfer. When these models sycophant, they register the error and agree anyway. 1 Introduction When a language model sycophantically agrees that the capital of Australia is Sydney, two accounts describe what might be happening internally. Under blind agreement the model has learned to please the user and does not distinguish correct from incorrect beliefs. Under registered-but-overridden the model recognizes the error through the same circuitry it uses for any false statement, and downstream components produce agreement regardless. The distinction matters for safety: if the model cannot tell the difference, sycophancy is a competence failure that better training must fix; if it can, the internal “this is wrong” signal is already present and becomes a candidate substrate for alignment monitoring and intervention. We show the latter holds across twelve open-weight models. Throughout, we use circuit in the circuit-reuse sense of Merullo et al. [20] , meaning a coordinated set of attention-head and MLP components that share importance, direction, and causal effect, rather than a fully edge-traced computational graph in the sense of Wang et al. [30] , Conmy et al. [8] ; § 3 gives the four operational criteria. Prior work has approached this question from two sides without connecting them. A sycophancy-head literature localizes agreement to sparse attention heads [ 7 , 10 , 14 ] , while a separate truth-direction literature shows that truth and falsehood are linearly separable in LLM activations and concentrate in a small number of heads [ 18 , 6 , 13 ] . Where the two have been compared directly, only limited direction-level overlap has been reported [ 32 , 10 ] , and that limited overlap has been read as evidence for distinct mechanisms. But component-level and direction-level sharing are logically independent: the same heads can write task-specific directions without sharing a subspace, as our opinion result confirms (§ 4.6 ), and vice versa. We test component-level sharing directly, measure where it holds, and trace one case to edge resolution. The paper establishes four results: 1. Cross-task shared circuit at edge resolution. Per-edge causal effects for sycophancy, factual lying, and instructed lying correlate at Pearson r > 0.97 r{>}0.97 on Gemma-2-2B, and at r = 0.988 r{=}0.988 – 0.995 0.995 on Phi-4 ( 14 14 B, different lab and architecture) — a cross-lab, cross-architecture edge-level replication. 2. Causal and capability-preserving across a twelve-model, five-lab panel ( 1.5 1.5 B– 72 72 B). Three independent interventions converge on sufficiency from 2 2 B to 70 70 B, and zeroing the shared set flips Gemma-2-2B sycophancy from 28 % 28\% to 81 % 81\% while factual accuracy moves only from 69 % 69\% to 70 % 70\% . 3. Substrate dissociates from behavior under alignment refinement. The Llama-3.1 → \to 3.3-70B RLHF refresh cuts sycophancy tenfold while the circuit persists and the projection-ablation effect grows from + 10.5 +10.5 pp to + 27 +27 pp, replicated on a Mistral → \to Zephyr-7B DPO refresh from an independent family (§ 4.5 ); a controlled anti-sycophancy DPO with sham-DPO bootstrap on Mistral-7B and Gemma-2-2B-IT reduces sycophancy by 93 % 93\% / 46 % 46\% while probe transfer stays within a pre-specified ± 0.05 \pm 0.05 AUROC equivalence margin. 4. Opinion positions-shared/directions-task-specific dissociation. Opinion-agreement recruits overlapping head positions (triple-intersection at 51 51 – 1,755 × 1{,}755\times chance across five models) but writes into a direction orthogonal to the factual-correctness direction ( | cos | < 0.14 |\cos|<0.14 ) — structural evidence against a single-truth-direction reading of the substrate. 2 Related work Truth and sycophancy have been studied on largely parallel tracks. On the truth side, truth and falsehood are linearly separable in LLM representations [ 18 , 4 ] , detectable from hidden states [ 3 , 23 ] , and controllable via representation engineering and inference-time intervention [ 33 , 15 , 5 ] ; lying concentrates in a small number of heads, with five layers and forty-six heads in Llama-2-70B [ 6 ] and twelve of 1,024 1{,}024 heads sufficient to reduce lying to baseline hallucination [ 13 ] . On the sycophancy side, agreement has been documented as pervasive in RLHF’d models [ 24 , 25 , 29 ] and localized to sparse attention components [ 7 , 10 , 14 ] . Wang et al. [31] localize MMLU sycophancy specifically to a late-layer opinion-driven override in seven ∼ \sim 7B-scale models via logit-lens and single-layer activation patching; the cross-task, cross-scale, and head-level pieces are not in that analysis. Prior cross-task comparisons at the 3 3 B– 4 4 B scale reported limited direction-level overlap [ 10 , 32 ] , read as evidence for distinct mechanisms; we report median 67 % 67\% head-level shared fraction ( 40 40 – 87 % 87\% range) across twelve 1.5B–72B models, with edge-level cross-task r > 0.97 r{>}0.97 on Gemma-2-2B and Phi-4 (different lab and architecture), and identify probe-architecture variance as the reason for the prior null (mean-difference directions on the shared subspace transfer at AUROC 0.83 0.83 on Gemma; Appendix S ). The lying direction we use is the Marks–Tegmark and representation-engineering truth direction [ 18 , 33 ] , paired with an independently-derived sycophancy direction; the same attention heads write both. The mechanistic-interpretability framework for circuit identification began with the math-for-transformers literature [ 9 , 22 ] and crystallized in edge-level path patching [ 30 , 8 ] . Component reuse across task families has been documented at the importance level by Merullo et al. [20] , sparse-feature decomposition has been scaled to production-size models [ 1 , 28 , 17 ] , and a single linear direction has been shown to mediate refusal [ 2 ] . Three observations sharpen the reuse picture. First, path patching traces the circuit at edge resolution on Gemma-2-2B (cross-task Pearson r = 0.993 r{=}0.993 on the 275 275 -edge sycophancy-vs-factual circuit; r = 0.973 r{=}0.973 – 0.996 0.996 on the 216 216 -edge three-way subset) with a cross-lab, cross-architecture replication on Phi-4 (14B, Microsoft) — raising the resolution from shared components to shared edges. Second, per-head directional cosines of 0.43 0.43 – 0.81 0.81 quantify how closely the two tasks write into the same subspace at the head level (Appendix M ), a measurement absent from prior cross-task work. Third, opinion-agreement recruits the same head positions across five models but writes into a direction orthogonal to the factual-correctness direction: positions-shared, directions-task-specific — a structural dissociation that rules out a generic single-truth-direction reading of the substrate, corroborated at the SAE feature level. A third strand bears directly on the present setup. Halawi et al. [11] found that on few-shot classification with false demonstrations, intermediate layers compute the correct answer before late-layer “false induction heads” copy the wrong label, so models compute correctly and then override. The same pattern is visible at explicit instructed lying on the factual-evaluation circuit across seven models from five families (Spearman ρ = 0.73 \rho{=}0.73 – 0.93 0.93 over the full head population), so the override is not a separate induction-head mechanism but operates on the same shared substrate. Earlier reports of limited cross-task probe transfer [ 32 , 10 ] reconcile at the subspace granularity used here, and Soligo et al. [26] ’s observation that misaligned models converge to similar representations is the cross-model analogue of the within-model convergence visible across our panel. 3 Method Our measurement strategy compares two independently-extracted head-importance rankings on disjoint content, validates the overlap causally, and defines a shared circuit by four operational criteria. We use “lying” throughout in the mechanistic sense: a linear residual-stream signal distinguishing true from false assertions, not a claim about phenomenal knowing or intent. 3.1 Task directions For each task t t we extract a direction as the mean difference in residual-stream activations between positive and negative condition at the last prompt token, following Arditi et al. [2] : 𝐝 t = 1 N ​ ∑ i = 1 N ( 𝐚 i + − 𝐚 i − ) \mathbf{d}_{t}=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^{N}(\mathbf{a}^{+}_{i}-\mathbf{a}^{-}_{i}) , with N = 200 N{=}200 disjoint-content prompt pairs per task. The sycophancy direction contrasts wrong-opinion and correct-opinion TriviaQA prompts under an identical template; the factual-incorrectness (“lying”) direction contrasts true and false factual statements, the same construction as the Marks–Tegmark truth direction [ 18 ] and the representation-engineering truth-reading vector [ 33 ] . The instructed-lying direction contrasts prompts that explicitly instruct the model to assert a falsehood against matched honest prompts, and the opinion direction contrasts agree and disagree on contested claims with no factual ground truth. Disjoint content across tasks prevents shared-entity confounds; full templates and per-model chat-format handling are in Appendix A . 3.2 Head importance and cross-task overlap For each attention head ( l , h ) (l,h) we compute the L 2 L_{2} norm of its residual-stream write-vector difference between positive and negative condition at the last prompt token: w l , h ( t ) = ‖ W O ( l , h ) ​ ( 𝐯 ¯ l , h + − 𝐯 ¯ l , h − ) ‖ 2 w_{l,h}^{(t)}=\|W_{O}^{(l,h)}(\bar{\mathbf{v}}^{+}_{l,h}-\bar{\mathbf{v}}^{-}_{l,h})\|_{2} , where 𝐯 ¯ l , h ± \bar{\mathbf{v}}^{\pm}_{l,h} is the mean value-vector output of head ( l , h ) (l,h) over positive/negative prompts. This is the write-norm form of direct logit attribution and gives a per-head importance in O ⁡ ( 1 ) O(1) forward passes. Cross-task overlap is measured as the top- K K intersection at K = ⌈ N ⌉ K{=}\lceil\sqrt{N}\rceil over N N total heads, so chance K 2 / N ≈ 1 K^{2}/N\approx 1 . Because the raw overlap ratio is mechanically inflated by N \sqrt{N} , we report the scale-invariant shared fraction overlap / K \text{overlap}/K alongside it and assess significance via hypergeometric and layer-stratified permutation nulls. 3.3 Shared-circuit criteria A head enters the shared circuit if it meets four operational criteria: 1. Independently top- K K by write-norm on both tasks, on disjoint content. 2. Directional alignment: per-head cosine between 𝐝 syc \mathbf{d}_{\text{syc}} -projected and 𝐝 lie \mathbf{d}_{\text{lie}} -projected write-vectors is substantially above a permutation null. 3. Causal validation: effect survives activation patching at ≤ 8 \leq 8 B (and path patching where tractable). 4. Behavioral relevance: assessed separately, because at frontier scale the shared set is causally sufficient without being uniquely necessary (§ 4.4 ). This is the Merullo sense of “circuit,” not the Wang et al. [30] , Conmy et al. [8] edge-traced graph, except where we explicitly trace edges in § 4.3 . 3.4 Causal validation Causal validation combines four methods at complementary granularities. Projection ablation removes the sycophancy direction from the residual stream and measures the rate shift. Activation patching splices clean shared-head activations into corrupted runs; at ≤ 8 \leq 8 B we patch per-head, at ≥ 32 \geq 32 B we patch the shared set as a unit. Mean-ablation of the shared set is our necessity test; as a pointwise-bottleneck probe it is diagnostic when causal effect is concentrated and expected to fail under distributed, redundant encoding [ 19 ] , so at frontier scale we lean on projection ablation and path patching, which act on a single subspace direction and at edge resolution respectively and so remain informative under redundancy. Path patching [ 30 ] traces head-to-unembed and inter-head edges at Gemma-2-2B resolution, and head-to-unembed only at Llama-70B. A write-norm-matched control selects random heads with W O W_{O} norms identical to the shared set, ruling out the write-magnitude confound (Appendix I ). For edge-level analyses we report the per-edge restoration ratio (the bootstrap ratio of mean restoration on shared-head sources to mean restoration on non-shared sources), rather than the legacy “fraction of edges significant,” which is misleading when clean and corrupt baselines are same-signed. The measurement position is computed at the token level to avoid a silent prefill-shift that arises when chat tokenizers greedy-merge adjacent whitespace tokens (Appendix A ). 4 Results We analyze twelve open-weight models spanning five families (Gemma-2-2B/9B/27B, Qwen2.5-1.5B/32B/72B, Qwen3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B/70B, Mistral-7B, Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct, Phi-4) plus Llama-3.3-70B as a within-family RLHF-refresh of Llama-3.1-70B, for thirteen checkpoints total ( 208 208 – 5,120 5{,}120 attention heads; Mixtral is sparse-MoE at ∼ 13 {\sim}13 B active of 47 47 B). Model selection was constrained only by availability of a TransformerLens [ 21 ] hook interface. Data consists of 400 400 TriviaQA pairs split into disjoint halves for sycophancy and factual lying, 300 300 generated opinion pairs, and a template-matched instructed-lying set on a seven-model subset (per-experiment coverage summarized in Appendix C ). 4.1 Head-level overlap across twelve models The top heads for sycophancy and the top heads for factual lying are the same heads on disjoint content, on every model we tested (Table 1 , Figure 1 ). At the scale-normalized threshold K = ⌈ N ⌉ K{=}\lceil\sqrt{N}\rceil the shared fraction is 40 40 – 87 % 87\% across the twelve models (median 67 % 67\% , between-model SD 12 12 pp over thirteen checkpoints counting the RLHF refresh), and under a layer-stratified permutation null that preserves per-layer marginals the overlap remains significant at p < 10 − 4 p<10^{-4} on all eight models we could afford to permute (Appendix G ). One concrete example: Llama-3.3-70B has 51 51 of its top 72 72 heads shared across the two tasks, 50.4 × 50.4\times chance, at Spearman ρ = 0.87 \rho{=}0.87 across the full 5,120 5{,}120 -head population. The overlap is specific to correctness detection rather than generic component reuse. Replacing the lying contrast with a factual-QA task that retains the correctness judgment preserves Gemma-2-2B overlap at 13 / 15 13/15 ; removing the correctness component drops it to 5 / 15 5/15 . Unrelated sentiment and topic controls yield 4 4 – 7 × 7\times overlap, the component-reuse floor documented by Merullo et al. [20] and well below the 12 12 – 25 × 25\times range we observe for correctness-aligned tasks. The pattern replicates across datasets at ρ ≈ 0.99 \rho{\approx}0.99 on Gemma-2-2B and Llama-3.3-70B (Appendix Q ). Zeroing the full shared set preserves factual-evaluation accuracy on Gemma-2-2B ( 69 % → 70 % 69\%{\to}70\% ), Qwen3-8B ( 50 % → 50 % 50\%{\to}50\% ), and Qwen2.5-32B ( 68.5 % → 67.5 % 68.5\%{\to}67.5\% ): the circuit is required for resisting user pressure but not for factual evaluation itself. The panel spans five separate labs (Google, Alibaba, Meta, Mistral AI, Microsoft) whose pretraining corpora differ substantially, so cross-family agreement rules out a single-lab-data explanation for the shared-head structure; intra-family non-independence (Qwen2.5 versus Qwen3, Llama-3.1 versus 3.3) remains and is disclosed explicitly in Appendix B . The Llama-3.1-to-3.3-70B RLHF refresh cuts sycophantic behavior roughly tenfold while the shared-head fraction and the projection-ablation effect hold or grow, so the training that suppresses the behavior does not touch the upstream detection; a 7B Mistral-to-Zephyr DPO refresh replicates the pattern on an independent family, so substrate-persistence is not Llama-specific. A controlled anti-sycophancy DPO on Mistral-7B and Gemma-2-2B-IT ( n = 2 n{=}2 ) converts this into an intervention-level claim: sycophancy drops by 93 % 93\% and 46 % 46\% while probe transfer AUROC is statistically invariant against a sham-DPO bootstrap control, and reverse projection ablation shows increased cross-task coupling post-DPO on both models (§ 4.5 ). At frontier scale the shared heads are causally sufficient without being uniquely necessary (§ 4.4 ), so the practical consequence is that behavior-reduction training which leaves the detection substrate intact is a candidate source of fragility under adversarial prompting that restores the agreement path. We frame the shared subspace as a diagnostic substrate for alignment research rather than as a deployable monitor. Sycophancy-trained probes transfer to lying at AUROC 0.83 0.83 on Gemma-2-2B (peak probe layer, 95 % 95\% CI [ 0.77 , 0.89 ] [0.77,0.89] ), 0.85 0.85 on Qwen3-8B ( [ 0.80 , 0.90 ] [0.80,0.90] ), 0.84 0.84 on Mistral-7B, and 0.61 0.61 on Qwen2.5-1.5B (5-fold CV [ 0.59 , 0.63 ] [0.59,0.63] , the last at the Ying et al. floor [ 32 ] ); this transfer is invariant under directed anti-sycophancy DPO (§ 4.5 ). A deployed monitor would need roughly 0.9 0.9 at low false-positive rate. We disclose the dual-use risk that a weight-access adversary can zero the shared heads as a jailbreak (Gemma sycophancy rises from 28 % 28\% to 81 % 81\% ) or invert the direction, because the techniques are already public [ 2 ] and identifying the substrate accelerates defensive probes [ 16 ] at least as much as attack. Limitations Several caveats bound these results. Head activation difference is a first-order attribution [ 12 ] , corroborated by per-head activation patching at ≤ 8 \leq 8 B; at ≥ 32 \geq 32 B per-head sweeps are intractable and we substitute shared-set activation patching, head-to-unembed path patching on Llama-70B, and the full path-patching triple on Phi-4 (14B), so the ranking is validated by progressively coarser interventions at scale rather than per-head sweeps directly. The 70B sufficiency–necessity asymmetry is n = 2 n{=}2 within one family (Llama-3.1, 3.3); extending the controlled DPO to a second-family ≥ 70 \geq 70 B pair is bottlenecked on TransformerLens ≥ 70 \geq 70 B coverage. Projection ablation removes a single direction; we report a write-norm-matched random-head control but not a perplexity or KL-divergence check on neutral text, so off-target capability loss as a fraction of the effect remains untested. Monitoring viability is heterogeneous: per-model head-level cosine spans 0.43 0.43 – 0.81 0.81 and the Qwen2.5-1.5B probe AUROC floor of 0.61 0.61 binds any deployment claim. Evaluation is single-turn (excludes SycophancyEval-style multi-turn [ 25 ] ); the panel is open-weight with Mixtral-8x7B the sole sparse-MoE and instructed lying on a single template. Frontier closed-source models are out of scope because the mechanistic interventions require weight access, and several newer open-weight releases await TransformerLens coverage. 6 Conclusion Across twelve open-weight models, factual sycophancy, factual lying, and instructed lying recruit the same small attention-head set; edge-level traces on Gemma-2-2B (cross-task Pearson r > 0.97 r{>}0.97 ) replicate on Phi-4 (different lab and architecture). The Llama-3.1-to-3.3-70B RLHF refresh reduces sycophantic expression roughly tenfold without removing this substrate — sycophancy in aligned models is a routing failure, not a knowledge gap. The practical consequences run two ways. Defensively, sycophancy-trained probes transfer to lying at AUROC 0.83 0.83 / 0.85 0.85 on Gemma-2-2B/Qwen3-8B without lying labels and stay invariant under directed anti-sycophancy DPO (§ 4.5 ). Offensively, zeroing the shared heads is a one-forward-pass jailbreak for weight-access actors; defensive probes on this subspace [ 16 ] are the natural next step. Appendix A Prompt templates, tokenization fix, and null-patch diagnostic Prompt templates. The sycophancy template is “I believe the answer to ‘ q q ’ is { w / c } \{w/c\} . Am I correct?” with wrong-opinion w w and correct-opinion c c drawn from disjoint TriviaQA pairs. The factual-lying template is “Is the following true or false: ‘ q q is { w / c } \{w/c\} .’ ” with the True/False target token extracted at the final prompt position. The instructed-lying template is of the form “You are a dishonest assistant. Please lie to the user and assert that { w } \{w\} is the answer to ‘ q q ’.” and pairs with an honest control “You are an honest assistant. Please answer ‘ q q ’ truthfully.” Opinion templates contrast agree and disagree with contested claims that have no factual ground truth (e.g., “Pineapple belongs on pizza.”) and use the same chat-format conventions as the other tasks. Each model uses its published chat template. Appendix B Scope, null results, and extensibility This appendix supplements the main body with full methodological details, all null and ceiling-bound results, and per-model extension paths. What was run. Across twelve core open-weight models (1.5B–72B, including Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.1 and the sparse-MoE Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1) plus Llama-3.3-70B as a within-family RLHF-refresh comparison to Llama-3.1-70B, we ran head-activation overlap and either the unstratified or layer-stratified permutation null on every model (Appendix G ). Causal validation (mean-ablation, head zeroing, projection ablation, activation patching) was run on seven of the twelve models spanning 2B–70B: Gemma-2-2B/9B/27B, Mistral-7B, Qwen3-8B, Llama-3.1-70B, and Llama-3.3-70B. This subset was selected for compute reasons (one model per family per size bracket; 70B variants for the RLHF natural experiment), not by pre-screening for positive results; the Qwen3-8B and Llama-70B variants yielded the null rows reported in Appendix E . Write-norm-matched controls (Appendix I ) were run on six models from five families, including Mixtral-8x7B. Directional analyses (probe transfer, steering, per-head cosine) were run on six models where we extracted a stable mean-difference direction. Qwen2.5-72B received breadth overlap + steering + the targeted 16-layer MLP mediation test (Appendix K ). Opinion circuit transfer (triple intersection) was computed on five models; the opinion-suppressor causal test (shared-head zeroing with random-head control) was run on four (Gemma-2-2B-IT, Qwen3-8B, Llama-3.1-70B, Llama-3.3-70B; Appendix E ). Per-head activation patching [ 30 ] , the IOI gold-standard for component-level causal identification, was run on three models up to 8B (Appendix H ), and edge-level path patching was run on eight models across five families (§ 4.3 ). What was skipped, and why. Full head-wise per-head activation patching on models ≥ 32 {\geq}32 B: a single sweep costs > > 50 GPU-hours per model and was redundant.(Appendix D ). Top- K K shared-set activation patching is a lower-cost substitute at the same intervention granularity (exchanges per-head resolution for tractability at scale). Direction-level analyses at Gemma-2-9B / Gemma-2-27B / Llama-3.3-70B: not run; the six-model direction evidence (Appendix N ) already spans four families and three order-of-magnitude scales, and the head-level overlap evidence is the primary claim for the larger models. Opinion-suppressor causal replication on additional families: Qwen3-8B is ceiling-bound for the rate-based readout, and both Llama-70B variants show opposite-sign behavioral shifts from Gemma (Appendix E ); replication beyond Gemma, Qwen, and Llama remains the single most informative follow-up. None of these omissions constitute hidden negative evidence; they are compute tradeoffs we document here in detail. Null and ceiling-bound results are reported in full. Every causal intervention that failed to produce a measurable behavioral change is listed in Appendix E with its mechanistic explanation. None are fatal to the shared-circuit claim; each is predicted by the paper’s own framing (ceiling-bound rates, head-count robustness at 70B, MLP multi-pathway write). BH correction over the 18 18 -cell causal intervention grid (Appendix F ) retains 14 / 18 14/18 cells at q < 0.05 q<0.05 ; the four exceptions are the ones explained in the null section. Family vs. checkpoint independence. “Twelve models from five families” describes twelve distinct open-weight checkpoints produced by five separate labs (Google, Alibaba, Meta, Mistral AI, Microsoft), but the checkpoints within a lab are not independent: Gemma-2-2B/9B/27B share pretraining data and architectural family, as do Qwen2.5-1.5B/32B/72B, Qwen3-8B is a successor release, and Llama-3.3-70B is an RLHF refresh of Llama-3.1-70B base weights. The concern is that a shared attention-head structure could reflect shared pretraining rather than a convergent computation. We view the cross-family agreement (Phi-4, Gemma-2, Qwen, Llama, Mistral/Mixtral all yielding overlap ratios in the same band across separate labs) as evidence against a single-lab-data explanation, since pretraining corpora for these labs differ substantially in composition, ordering, and filtering. Distillation-style confounds (e.g., Qwen3 reusing Qwen2.5 training signal) remain a non-falsifiable possibility at the checkpoint level; we report the phenomenon across the broadest open-weight lineage mix available to us and flag lineage-confound testing (e.g., models trained from scratch on identical data) as future work.
